steps: Draw operand muxes, ALU function, register/memory write enables and PC selection. Implement next-state independently of commit, and annotate fetch/decode/operand/execute/update for each event. Inspect source for accidental same-step read-after-update and test a source/destination alias case.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: 1. Record exact board revision, Ethernet pins/solder bridges, PHY address/ID and 50 MHz reference source. Measure the clock with adequate instrument bandwidth/sampling.

A PHY status fault cannot be inferred solely from a synthetic adapter timeout.

requires_reasons.LAB-EX-07: Continue the same implementation with its established contract.

steps: 1. Spend the first 4 h defining sender/receiver tuple and states, checked fragment arithmetic and matching ACK rules; run a normal 25-octet transfer.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Reliable bounded transport and flow state.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Retain the sender/receiver state diagram, exact fragment/ACK ledger, injected-clock log, complete upper bytes and failure cleanup witnesses. For all three objectives show checked segmentation/reassembly, match/retry/credit transitions and absence of partial publication/leaks. Capture one dropped-ACK retry on the bench if available. An eventual successful transfer alone cannot replace the timeout/duplicate evidence.

A mismatched ACK frees nothing. Duplicate accepted data appends nothing. Wrong non-final length, unexpected index/count, total over 120, old completed ID, unsupported port and no capacity are distinct rejects. Credit probes do not restart the blocked deadline. At retry or blocked failure, clear partial state and publish a failure event, never a partial SDU. Session reopen clears old receipts and separates ID incarnations.

checks: For .a provide the exact sequence, largest actual cost 9 and total 27. For .b submit all prefix credit/potential rows and the initial-state variant. For .c state that this is a deterministic worst-case sequence guarantee under unit-copy assumptions, not an expectation over random arrivals. Attach actual prior-table callback/count traces and the preserved failure case. The independent oracle verifies these finite rows and transient payload capacity, not the implementation's allocator time or total process memory.

A long single growth operation remains expensive even when the sequence average is bounded. Shrink, concurrent mutation, allocator latency and destruction are outside this expansion-only model and must not inherit its guarantee.

checks: For .a submit an original hand-traced stream and the N/M/B/D/P model contract. For .b submit all read/write/useful byte totals, ratios and null denominator case. For .c supply actual existing-adapter observations or a clearly labeled denied device-accounting boundary, plus a warm-state explanation and follow-up. The independent Python model checks the bounded policy, not C correctness on every stream or a physical device model.

Reject invalid indices, unknown read/write modes and geometry that violates the stated buffer contract. The empty stream must not divide by zero. A dirty hit does not write back immediately in this policy. A bus transaction, disk I/O and CPU cache fill can have different sizes; replacing one with another invalidates the unit label.

units.title: Build and inspect: Read/write performance and persistence

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: 1. Add a response seam to the existing adapter and record remaining range, positive accepted count, errno policy and attempt limit. Verify output bytes have neither duplication nor gaps.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Read/write performance and persistence.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: For .a provide scripted traces and actual final byte checks, including terminal/zero/retry cases. For .b submit separate native buffered and synchronization samples with file lifetime/warm-state protocol. For .c submit file/device/return-boundary reconciliation and the persistence limits. The independent oracle certifies scripted counts and phase arithmetic only. Native fsync success is evidence of the requested OS boundary, not experimental proof of crash/power-loss durability.

A positive transfer consumes only that many remaining bytes. EINTR in this seam means no bytes transferred by that attempt. Stop terminal EIO and preserve progress; a later successful read cannot erase the error. read returning zero is EOF, while this bounded write adapter treats zero as no progress. Successful write alone is not requested durability; successful file fsync does not prove directory-entry synchronization or survival of every failure mode.

checks: For .a provide scripted traces and actual final byte checks, including terminal/zero/retry cases. For .b submit separate native buffered and synchronization samples with file lifetime/warm-state protocol. For .c submit file/device/return-boundary reconciliation and the persistence limits. The independent oracle certifies scripted counts and phase arithmetic only. Native fsync success is evidence of the requested OS boundary, not experimental proof of crash/power-loss durability.

checks: For .a submit the actual hierarchy/controller/delegation inventory or denied record and policy/accounting classification. units.title: Build and inspect: Bare-metal cycle and timer measurement

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: 1. Read the exact DDI0403E.e DEMCR/DWT scopes and selected-device/core identity. DEMCR at 0xE000EDFC has TRCENA bit 24; DWT_CTRL at 0xE0001000 has NOCYCCNT bit 25/CYCCNTENA bit 0; CYCCNT is at 0xE0001004. Access through the already accepted implementation's MMIO contract. Presence/access/errata/clock are implementation checks, not assumptions from these addresses.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Bare-metal cycle and timer measurement.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: For .a supply the manual/device/access/setup ownership checklist and absent/unknown route. For .b derive the 64-cycle case, units, ambiguous-wrap rejection and overhead sensitivity; give an independently justified interval bound for any actual trial. For .c submit the labeled core captured/static certificate and timer/GPIO comparison, or add silicon evidence with all firmware preludes satisfied. No core pass certifies a physical board, energy or WCET. The finite oracle verifies scope flags and arithmetic, not memory-mapped register behavior.

Reject an out-of-width endpoint, nonboolean feature flag, unknown clock or bound admitting a full wrap. The core counter is optional and may be inaccessible; those results must not become zero cycles. Debug state stops CYCCNT, so a halted span cannot be converted into full wall elapsed time. An overhead subtraction at or below overhead is inconclusive. Interrupt cycles, clock changes and probe effects remain in scope unless independently controlled.

steps: 2. Before opening the withheld oracle, commit predictions, a bounded replay, two hypotheses, first-invalid-state evidence and a repair. Reveal the oracle only after submitting the dossier, replay neighbor/regression cases and request feedback. Repeat after seven days with a different variant; a solo seed must remain unopened until the attempt.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Causal repair, regression and delayed blind transfer.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

units.title: Build and inspect: Timer preemption with a nonpreemptible kernel

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.
requires_reasons.U-T04-01-04: Import bytes.checked: Finite-width arithmetic reports overflow before changing output; division edge cases declared.

steps: Configure the pinned PC timer/PIC, issue end-of-interrupt, retain each process frame, switch CR3 and kernel-stack ownership, then return to the next user. Separate explicit yield from timer-caused switches.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Timer preemption with a nonpreemptible kernel.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Two CPU-consuming workers that never call yield complete after observed timer ticks; their private memory values survive. Record timer-driven switches and nonpreemptible sections.
No EOI, switching to a dead process, using another process kernel stack, dropping a register, confusing syscall frequency with cooperative yield and claiming hard real-time behavior from QEMU ticks.

units.title: Build and inspect: Feedback and proportional-share scheduling

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.
requires_reasons.U-T49-03-04: Explicit project contract consumes the prior FCFS, SJF, SRTF and round-robin scheduling capability.

steps: Add a three-level MLFQ with explicit allotments, periodic boost and yield accounting, then stride scheduling with weights1:2:4. Compare interactive bursts, a CPU hog and a yield-gaming worker.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Feedback and proportional-share scheduling.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Show the boost prevents the declared starvation case and service converges toward the selected weight ratios over a finite long run. Document transient error and distinguish this teaching policy from Linux EEVDF.
allotment reset on every yield; starving low queue; zero weight; pass overflow; unfair tie-breaking; sleeping worker receiving unbounded credit.

steps: Implement the four policies and print each eviction. Use reference string1,2,3,4,1,2,5,1,2,3,4,5 with three and four frames to examine FIFO anomaly.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for U-T50-05-03: Which timer representation fits this task bound? Compare sorted deadline list versus binary min-heap. Measure insertion/cancellation and worst traversal at the declared task count.
Implement a bounded deadline queue with stable equal-deadline ordering and generation-checked cancellation. Compare phase-preserving periodic release with delay-after-work using a fake clock.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Timers and an absolute-deadline queue.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Demonstrate releases at10,20,30 for phase-preserving scheduling despite varying work duration, and explain drift in the alternative. Preserve rollover and cancellation traces.
clock wrap; already-due deadline; simultaneous expiry; canceled timer reused; zero delay; requested distance at or beyond half range.

phases.title: Trustworthy small tools
phases.gate: Bounded record tool, checked input, explicit errors and repaired regressions.

phases.title: A portable toolbox
phases.gate: Bytes, containers, parsers, storage policies and algorithms shared by two consumers.

phases.title: Crossing execution boundaries
phases.gate: Actual files, pipes, processes and reset/UART adapters explain machine and OS boundaries.

phases.title: Responsive communicating systems
phases.gate: Telemetry and HTTP tolerate segmentation, overload, deadlines and shutdown.

phases.title: Original concurrent execution
phases.gate: Cooperative contexts, preemption, synchronization, scheduling and early protected execution.

phases.title: Programmable and durable components
phases.gate: Hosted VM and recoverable store reuse representations, allocation and fault harnesses.

phases.title: Multiple processors and ownership
phases.gate: SMP and AMP revalidate publication, cache/DMA visibility and reclamation separately.

phases.title: Composed protected systems
phases.gate: The same VM/store and protocol components operate across process and target boundaries.

phases.title: Architectural revision and defense
phases.gate: Changed requirements force a justified migration and new independent evidence.
